statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON (green). Tail sits in the low band at 16% while Stress is elevated at 51%.
recommendation: Tail remains well below the block threshold, so the deterministic mapping stays at EA_ON. The only interval in the horizon reaching the watch band is the 19:00Z-20:15Z quadruple-witching settlement window, which is flagged as a narrow mechanical-flow checkpoint rather than a session-wide condition.
headline: NQ holds 29,735.75 mid-band with the 29,966.75 overnight high unretaken, cash NDX 29,456.19 recovered off a 29,407.28 low, and the 10-year touched 5.00% while VIX 15.33 and semis +1.26% pull the other way into quadruple-witching settlement
body: Nasdaq-100 futures print 29,735.75 inside a 29,648.00-29,966.75 session band, effectively unchanged on the day at -0.02%, while cash NDX trades 29,456.19 against a 29,446.98 previous close after opening at 29,529.64. The structural read is why Tail stays in the low band and eases a point from the prior hour. The overnight high at 29,966.75 has now stood unretaken for roughly eight hours. The cash session opened higher, extended to 29,560.30, failed, sold through to a 29,407.28 low and has since recovered to positive territory. That is a completed two-way rotation: pullbacks are not shallow, retracements are not failing, and price is trading inside the band rather than extending from it. The specific amplifier that preceded the strategy's worst historical sessions, opening-auction continuation to new highs, did not appear. Two scheduled US items printed this morning and both were soft. August industrial production, released at 13:15Z and verified from the Federal Reserve G.17, was unchanged on the month with manufacturing output down 0.3% and capacity utilisation at 76.3%. The Conference Board Leading Economic Index for August, released at 14:00Z, receded 0.1% to 99.5, its first monthly decline since March. Against a Federal Reserve that lifted the target range to 3.75-4.00% on Wednesday and signalled a further increase this year, that combination produces dispersion rather than direction. Cross-assets do not form an amplifier stack; they conflict. VIX trades 15.33 in a 14.99-15.61 range against a 17.71 previous close, so the post-decision volatility crush is intact and is not confirming any stress-driven decline. The 10-year yield at 5.00%, up about 6 basis points in a 4.97-5.01 range, is the genuine conflict and sits exactly on the level that has framed equity risk appetite since the decision; H.15 put the 2-year and 10-year constant maturities at 4.74% and 5.01% on 16 September. The PHLX Semiconductor Index is 1.26% higher at 11,745.86 while the index itself is flat, a rotation divergence that lowers directional conviction without adding path risk. Crude has re-firmed rather than eased: WTI pared earlier losses to about 102.2 dollars, up 0.27%, after satellite imagery showed three pumping stations on Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline damaged with uncertain repair timelines and Aramco notified at least two European refining customers that they will receive no crude next month. That is a modest re-tightening of the supply channel against yesterday's easing narrative, and it raises Stress rather than Tail because equities are not transmitting it. The dominant mode is mixed. The identifiable conditional risk for the remainder of the session is mechanical rather than informational. September quadruple-witching settles at the 20:00Z cash close, with around 7 trillion dollars notional expiring today in the second-largest such event on record. Citadel Securities put roughly 60% of that expiry at the opening rotation, which has already cleared without disorder, but the residual plus closing pin risk still concentrates into the settlement print, where closing volume historically runs several times a normal session. That flow can briefly overwhelm mean reversion, which is why the danger window is drawn narrowly at 19:00Z-20:15Z rather than across the whole afternoon. Shared Finviz cross-asset context was read at the start of this run but carried a 11:53Z collection time, roughly 212 minutes old, with partial coverage and no futures or calendar section, so it was treated as unhealthy and this assessment rests entirely on independently verified sources. Beyond the futures close at 21:00Z the tape is shut until Sunday, so the later forecast hours describe a dormant market in which no price path can develop.

lookbackSummary: The last 24 published hours cover a complete transition. Thursday afternoon ran with Tail in the 20-24 watch band and a trend-up mode as the post-decision relief rally extended, with Stress decaying from 53% toward the mid-40s as the volatility crush progressed. From 22:00Z the assessment moved to green with a normal mode and Tail in the 17-18 area through the Asian and European sessions. Tail ticked to 19% during the European morning as futures firmed, then eased to 15-17% from 11:00Z as the overnight high was left behind and the mode was reclassified to mixed. Stress has held in the upper 40s to low 50s through the European and US hours, reflecting the yield and crude backdrop rather than realised index volatility.
outlookSummary: The forecast holds Tail in the low band at 16-18% through the US cash afternoon on the assumption that the observed two-way band behaviour persists, then lifts it to 22% and 21% for the 19:00Z and 20:00Z hours containing the September quadruple-witching settlement, where mechanical expiration flow rather than new information is the identified risk. Those two hours are the only part of the horizon reaching the watch band and the only interval covered by the danger window. From 21:00Z the futures session closes for the week, so Tail falls to 13% and then toward a 5-8% structural floor across the closed weekend hours, while Stress decays into the low band and Confidence declines steadily with distance from the last observed price path. The horizon ends before the Sunday reopen, so the next assessment will be rebuilt on freshly observed structure.
